brief.headline: KOSPI whipsaw continues: Samsung/Hynix bounce 8-15% after 10% Monday rout; HBM/NAND pricing supercycle intact despite vol spike
brief.summary: <cite index="38-2,38-5">Samsung closed down 10.18% at 295,500 won on June 8, while SK Hynix fell 7.68% to 1,911,000 won.</cite> <cite index="42-1,42-9">Both rebounded sharply June 9, with Samsung up over 8% and SK Hynix surging over 15% to 2.2 million won.</cite> <cite index="38-9,38-12,38-13">Brokerages dismissed the move as short-term profit-taking after the rally, keeping target prices unchanged and calling the pullback a buying opportunity.</cite> <cite index="12-2,12-7,12-8">DRAM contract prices rose 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, while NAND jumped 70-75% QoQ, following Q1's record 90-95% DRAM and 55-60% NAND increases.</cite> <cite index="21-5,21-9">The four hyperscalers collectively plan to spend roughly $700 billion on capex in 2026, nearly double 2025 levels.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: SK Hynix holds structural edge on HBM3E/4 leadership and tighter Nvidia allocation discipline. <cite index="1-24">UBS predicts SK Hynix will achieve approximately 70% market share in HBM4 for Nvidia's Rubin platform in 2026.</cite> <cite index="39-1,39-4,39-5">SK Hynix announced a multi-year partnership to supply advanced memory to Nvidia on June 9, boosting shares 10.6%.</cite> Samsung is still proving HBM4 qualification but benefits from dual memory/foundry optionality and recent LP40/advanced packaging commentary. <cite index="4-12">Samsung's co-CEO stated customers have said 'Samsung is back' on HBM4, though SK Hynix held 53% HBM market share in Q3 2025 versus Samsung's 35%.</cite> Near-term, favor SK Hynix on momentum and supply visibility; Samsung offers beta leverage if foundry diversification accelerates. Watch relative ETF flows—retail piled into 2T+ won of leveraged single-stock products last week, amplifying Monday's selloff but signaling sticky positioning.

memory_cycle.stage: Mid-supercycle expansion with structural supply deficit through 2027
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="1-11">BofA forecasts global DRAM revenue to surge 51% and NAND 45% YoY in 2026, with ASPs rising 33% and 26% respectively.</cite> <cite index="3-1">Goldman Sachs forecasts a 4.9% DRAM supply deficit in 2026.</cite> <cite index="6-23">Each gigabyte of HBM consumes roughly three times the wafer capacity of DDR5.</cite> <cite index="11-6">Server DRAM prices projected to rise more than 60% QoQ in Q1 2026.</cite> <cite index="14-7">Analysts project the memory price rally is poised to extend past 2028.</cite> Pricing parabolic but structurally supported by hyperscaler pre-buys, HBM wafer displacement, and new fab delays to late 2027/2028.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-15">BofA estimates the 2026 HBM market to reach $54.6 billion, a 58% increase from 2025.</cite> <cite index="6-1,6-25">SK Hynix, the largest HBM supplier to Nvidia, has told investors its advanced packaging lines are at capacity through 2026.</cite> <cite index="4-3">Samsung is expanding HBM production capacity by around 50% in 2026, while SK Hynix plans to increase infrastructure investment more than fourfold.</cite> <cite index="1-18,1-19">HBM3E is expected to remain the flagship product in 2026, with Nvidia's Blackwell Ultra, Google, and AWS selecting HBM3E for ASIC-based AI chips.</cite> <cite index="1-20,1-21,1-23">SK Hynix secured the world's first mass production system for HBM4 in September 2025 and is expected to support both HBM3E and HBM4 by 2026.</cite> Alternative architectures emerging: <cite index="9-4,9-5,9-6">Korean memory manufacturers are discussing placing GPUs and HBM in separate packages connected through optical links, potentially allowing GPUs to support several times more HBM than existing designs.</cite>

news_pulse.headline: Samsung/SK Hynix rebound 8-15% after 10% Monday selloff; KOSPI circuit breaker triggered
news_pulse.implication: Extreme vol in leveraged ETFs and retail capitulation signal positioning flush; brokerages holding target prices. Near-term tradeable bounce but watch for secondary test if hyperscaler earnings disappoint.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix announces multi-year Nvidia partnership for advanced memory supply
news_pulse.implication: Confirms HBM3E/4 allocation lock-in through 2027+; reinforces SK's structural moat vs Samsung. Likely includes HBM4 prepayments and volume commitments.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex revised to $700B (up from $670B pre-earnings); BofA sees $800B+
news_pulse.implication: Sustained GPU/HBM pull despite FCF compression. Amazon $200B, Alphabet $175-185B, Meta $115-135B, Microsoft $190B. Demand visibility intact through H2.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity hits 130,000 wafers/month by late 2026 (up from 35k in late 2024)
news_pulse.implication: Packaging bottleneck easing but Nvidia locked 60% allocation; AMD/Broadcom fighting for scraps. HBM die supply now critical path—benefits SK/Samsung.

news_pulse.headline: Q2 2026 DRAM prices +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75% QoQ per TrendForce
news_pulse.implication: ASP momentum accelerating sequentially; NAND now outpacing DRAM for first time. Enterprise SSD tightness structural through 2027; eMMC/UFS lowest priority.

news_pulse.headline: BofA forecasts DRAM revenue +51% YoY, NAND +45% in 2026; names SK Hynix 'Top Pick'
news_pulse.implication: Supercycle narrative entrenched; SK positioned as primary beneficiary. 2026 memory market size could exceed $440B per industry estimates.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung/SK Hynix reviewing AI packaging fabs in Honam region; govt meeting this month
news_pulse.implication: Advanced packaging expansion accelerating domestically; sites in Gwangju/Jangseong. Competition with TSMC on HBM integration intensifies.

news_pulse.headline: Goldman forecasts 4.9% DRAM supply deficit in 2026; shortages may persist to 2027-28
news_pulse.implication: Structural undersupply validates elevated pricing. New fab capacity (Samsung P5, SK M15X) not online until mid-2027/2028.

brief.derivatives_signal: Extreme single-stock leverage ETF vol: 5 Samsung 2x products each down ~20% Monday; SK Hynix 2x down ~16%. <cite index="40-13,40-14,40-15">Retail net-purchased 2.08T won of TIGER SK Hynix Single-Stock Leverage and 1.46T won of TIGER Samsung Single-Stock Leverage within 7 trading days of listing.</cite> <cite index="38-27,38-28,38-29">229 domestic ETFs hold Samsung (51T won), 213 hold SK Hynix (46.2T won); the two stocks account for nearly 20% of Korea's 500T won ETF market.</cite> Mechanical bid/offer from rebalancing likely amplified Monday's move and today's bounce. Options skew likely elevated; premium to fade if spot stabilizes. Watch for forced deleveraging if names re-test lows.
